ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A square flag has a red cross of uniform width with a blue square in the center on a white background as shown. (The cross is symmetric with respect to each of the diagonals of the square.) If the entire cross (both the red arms and the blue center) takes up $36\%$ of the area of the flag, what percent of the area of the flag is blue?

method.method_draft: Use an analytic-coordinate strip model. First read the image as a square flag containing two equal-width diagonal bands crossing in an X shape; the four red regions are the parts of the bands outside their overlap, and the blue central diamond-shaped square is exactly the overlap of the two bands. Let the flag have side length 1. Let each diagonal band be described by an offset parameter a from its central diagonal, so one band is |x-y| <= a and the other is |x+y-1| <= a. From the text, the union of the two bands has area 0.36. Compute the area of one diagonal strip in the unit square as 2a - a^2, and compute the blue overlap area as 2a^2. By inclusion-exclusion, total cross area = 2(2a - a^2) - 2a^2 = 4a(1-a). Set 4a(1-a)=0.36, choose the small feasible width a=0.1, then blue area = 2a^2 = 0.02, so the blue part is 2%.

method.method_draft: Use the white-complement triangles instead of adding strips.
